explanation: Ran the prebuilt eta/build/exclurad binary with standard CLAS12 settings (model=3 EtaMAID/maid2000, full O(alpha) RC mode, bmom=6.53 GeV electron beam, fixed target, recoil proton detected (ivec=1), vcut=0.166 GeV^2 inelasticity cut) for the single point W=1.54 GeV, Q2=1.3207 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0.341379, phi*=36 deg. Note: the executable ignores stdin and always reads its input from a hardcoded 'input.dat' in the working directory (open(unit=5,file='input.dat') in exclurad.F), so input.dat was temporarily overwritten with this single-point request, run, then restored to its original template content afterward; the exact file used is saved as eta/input_used_W1.54_Q2_1.3207_cos0.341379_phi36.dat. The requested kinematic point is physically valid (W=1.54 GeV is above the eta+p threshold of ~1.486 GeV, Q2 and W are within the EtaMAID-2023 table grid, and phi* has no kinematic restriction). The Born cross section sigma_Born was computed successfully and is reported exactly as written by EXCLURAD in radtot.dat (column 7, F16.10 format): 0.0008651649. However, the radiative correction factor delta (column 6 of radtot.dat, ratio of radiated to Born cross section) came out as NaN, reproducibly (rerun gave the identical NaN), because the deterministic bremsstrahlung tail integral (subroutine qqt, d01fce integration over cos/phi/v near the kinematic peaking region around cos2) returned NaN for one of its sub-intervals (logged in eta/run.log as 'tai: 2 1 NaN NaN', 10329 evaluations, ifail=0) at this exact kinematic point. This is a numerical failure of the tail-integration routine near a phase-space singularity structure, not a sign that the kinematics themselves are unphysical -- the README notes this class of instability occurs 'near the eta threshold or large |cos theta*|' and recommends an unphysical-skip runner (not present in this repository copy) to detect and retry/skip such points. Because EXCLURAD did not produce a valid number for delta at this point, delta is reported as null per instructions.
